title: Sheep Kaomoji Ꮚ˘ꈊ˘Ꮚ: Copy & Paste Sheep and Lamb Faces
meta_description: Copy sheep kaomoji and lamb text faces: Ꮚ˘ꈊ˘Ꮚ with floppy ears, ᏊᵕꈊᵕᏊ smiling, @^ェ^@ in a woolly coat, ξ๑ˊꈊˋ๑Ҙ rams and soft ૮꒰ ˶• ༝ •˶꒱ა lambs.
hero_tagline: Woolly sheep, curly-horned rams and small lambs typed in text. Tap a face to copy it.
intro: Most sheep kaomoji are built on the Cherokee letter Ꮚ, which hangs down on both sides of the face like a pair of floppy sheep ears. Between them sits ꈊ, a Yi syllable shaped like a small split muzzle, so Ꮚ˘ꈊ˘Ꮚ reads as a sheep chewing calmly. Older Japanese faces take a different route and wrap the face in @ signs for curly wool, as in @^ェ^@. Swap the ears for ξ and Ҙ and the sheep grows ram horns. Ꮚ and ꈊ come from scripts that some older phones and desktop fonts lack, so a few readers may see empty boxes; the @ wool faces use only common characters. The 🐑 sheep and 🐏 ram emoji are on the animal emoji page.

faq.q: What is the Ꮚ character in sheep kaomoji?
faq.a: Ꮚ is the Cherokee letter TSI (U+13CA). Its curved sides look like ears hanging down, so kaomoji makers use it on both sides of a face to draw a sheep.

faq.q: Why do some sheep faces show boxes instead of letters?
faq.a: Ꮚ is Cherokee and ꈊ comes from the Yi syllables block. A device without a font for either script shows a box. The @^ェ^@ style uses Japanese katakana and basic symbols, which nearly every phone supports.

faq.q: How do I tell a ram from a sheep in text?
faq.a: Rams get horns: ξ on the left and Ҙ on the right curl outward, as in ξ๑ˊ ꈊˋ๑Ҙ. Plain sheep keep the hanging Ꮚ ears.
